caption_recommended: No vows yet. Bas habits ne thoda jaldi decide kar liya. 🤍
caption_alt: Officially, not married. Unofficially, every plan, problem, fight and check-in already comes in plural.
alt_text: Illustrated carousel slide 1: Wide three-quarter apartment doorway scene: Aachu slips Zuv's wallet and keys into his waiting jacket pocket while Zuv simultaneously lowers her filled water bottle into her open tote. Neither looks at the other; their crossed forearms and automatic timing prove muscle memory. Couple in lower half, clean ivory negative space above-left, brandmark clear top-right.

Illustrated carousel slide 2: Over-shoulder threshold view from outside: Aachu is halfway through the exit, one palm raised to the unseen outside world in a natural one-second gesture, while turning back toward Zuv. Zuv stands several feet inside holding two helmets and gives a familiar nod. The check-in reads as alignment, never permission.

Illustrated carousel slide 3: Wide profile hallway scene: Zuv holds a small blank framed print against the wall while Aachu stands several feet back, squinting with mock seriousness and pinching two fingers to signal two centimetres left. Their eye-lines converge on the frame; subtle painter's-tape alternatives show mutual over-investment without clutter.

Illustrated carousel slide 4: Tight over-Zuv-shoulder landing shot at lock level: he remains upright, frozen at the apartment lock, holding half of a snapped key while the other half is unmistakably stuck. Aachu is not yet visible. The solitary reaction establishes one person's problem before it spreads.

Illustrated carousel slide 5: High three-quarter landing view: the broken key remains in the lock. Both stay upright. Aachu searches her tote for a spare or maintenance number while Zuv lights the lock with his phone torch and examines it without forcing it. Their shoulders nearly touch and both eye-lines fix on the same obstacle; neither rescues the other.

Illustrated carousel slide 6: Low-medium two-shot along the same landing: Aachu holds out a blank maintenance card while Zuv holds the snapped key and argues for another solution. They stand two to three feet apart with direct eye-line, equal irritation, open palms, and no finger-pointing. The failed lock sits between their competing solutions.

Illustrated carousel slide 7: Wide view from inside the now-open doorway toward the stairwell: Zuv is already two steps down, body facing away with helmet in hand. Aachu remains in the doorway, posture still stiff, but instinctively calls after him. He stops mid-step and turns back immediately; their eye-lines reconnect across the distance.

Illustrated carousel slide 8: Intimate waist-up profile at the threshold: both still look mildly annoyed and avoid a romantic gaze. Aachu notices a tiny nick on Zuv's thumb from the broken key and offers a tissue while Zuv keeps his other arm completely outside the frame; no hand touches or braces the door. Zuv stands fully in front of the door and doorframe; a continuous visible contour separates his hair, shoulder, back, shirt, and torso from both solid surfaces. No door or frame line touches, crosses, replaces, or absorbs any part of his body. Their simultaneous gestures show anger and concern occupying the same frame; their hands nearly meet without an embrace.

Illustrated carousel slide 9: Very wide architectural landing shot: Aachu stands inside her doorway and Zuv pauses several steps away near the stairs, still connected by eye-line and each holding one of the other's everyday belongings. The physical space honestly shows two separate lives; the exchanged objects show the unofficial unit already operating.

Illustrated carousel slide 10: Circular visual echo of slide 1 on another morning and in different clothes: at the same doorway, Aachu passes Zuv his wallet while Zuv passes her water bottle in the same automatic crossed-hand relay. This time a repaired key hangs quietly beside the door and both share the smallest knowing smile. The visual closes the story through repeated behavior, not a wedding symbol or generic embrace.
